The wide version of the same sheet: all 41 districts of Rajasthan and the 36 districts of Pakistan, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat that share its border, laid out horizontally so the long international border reads without turning the page. Pakistan's bordering districts (Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Ghotki, Khairpur, Sanghar, Sukkur, Tharparkar, Umer Kot) and Rajasthan's own border belt — Barmer, Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Jaisalmer, Phalodi — sit along the top edge. Hindi labels, colour-coded state boundaries, north arrow and a 0–150 km scale bar; sized for a normal A4 printer and useful for RPSC, REET, Police, SI and Patwari revision.

One printable sheet shows all 41 districts of Rajasthan together with the 36 districts that share its border: Pakistan (Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan in Punjab province; Ghotki, Khairpur, Sanghar, Sukkur, Tharparkar, Umer Kot in Sindh) plus the bordering districts of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Districts of Rajasthan that touch Pakistan — Barmer, Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Jaisalmer and Phalodi — are the ones drawn along the international border.
